heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

REGENT OF SUKOHARJO

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKOHARJO REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is a form of execution of protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
18. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
19. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
21. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
22. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
23. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
24. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutional

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

In providing protection to victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by Integrated Services.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Integrated Services

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

1. Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 are established by the Regional Government in accordance with laws and regulations.
2. The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional personnel, volunteer assistants, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.
3. The Minimum Service Operational Standards for Integrated Services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

translated_text:
Part Three

Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Prevention Efforts

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 8 letter a include:
a. organizing communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Recovery and Social Reintegration Efforts

heading: Article 11
Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Legal Protection

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Legal protection as referred to in Article 8 letter c includes:
a. providing protection in safe houses (shelters);
b. providing assistance in legal processes; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence which can be carried out by appointing guardianship in accordance with applicable regulations.

Monitoring and Reporting

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 8 letter f includes monitoring, documentation and evaluation of cases of gender-based violence and violence against children.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

The implementation of integrated services is coordinated by the relevant SKPD.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

COOPERATION

Article 17

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the regional government cooperates with the Government, Provincial Government and District/City Government and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and District/City as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of Integrated Service System development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

ASSISTANCE

Article 18

Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with Integrated Services.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 19

1. Control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children is carried out by the Regent.
2. The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out on a daily basis by the relevant SKPD.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FINANCING

Article 20

All activities related to the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children are charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget as well as other legitimate and non-binding receipts.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 21

Integrated Service Institutions that violate the service principles as referred to in Article 9 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 22

Matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation insofar as they concern technical implementation shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sukoharjo Regency.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKOHARJO REGENCY

NUMBER 6 OF 2011 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL.
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKOHARJO REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honour, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in community, national and state life.

To realize the achievement of the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, whether in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in situations of peace or conflict. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKOHARJO REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, appropriate and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Letter f
What is meant by "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

Letter g
What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter h
What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter i
What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j
What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Letter k
What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Letter l
What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of the victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.
